passage.quote:
A separate binary64 PTX backend runs the repeated matrix-free operator and
conjugate-gradient arithmetic on the GPU, using the Lean reference for mesh,
quadrature, load and diagonal setup. Its empirical comparison, memory checks
and execution evidence are distinct from a formal PTX correspondence theorem.

summary: Run the matrix-free Poisson operator and PCG iterations in binary64 PTX using mesh, quadrature, load and diagonal setup supplied by Lean.
Use disjoint element storage and one writer per global node for deterministic ordered assembly without floating-point atomics.
Certify accepted solutions with an exact residual checker for the represented coefficients; retain separate instruction-correspondence obligations.
Prove whole-cell tensor correspondence from actual gathering, all eight contractions, barrier visibility and publication of computed stores.
Prove complete assembly entry correctness and general returning execution from valid arrays, including boundary masking and inactive-thread return.
Derive assembly read visibility from one joint history and prove its published ordered scatter; construct admitted returning parallel witnesses for arbitrary valid inputs.
Connect the complete true_residual kernel to its subtraction specification under explicit byte-source constraints.
Check emitted entries and launch shapes against Lean representations, preserving numerical order and the distinction between proof checking and GPU observations.
Compose actual cell publications with assembly using checked ordered input tables, preserving uploaded metadata and the TorchLean operator result.
Connect unmasked PTX cell/assembly publication directly to the public array-based TorchLean reference, preserving its validation and rounded scatter order.

Keep arbitrary-input whole-cell existence, serialized setup representation, remaining PCG/reduction instructions, launch composition, complete PTX admission and hardware conformance as separate obligations.
Interleave actual cell instructions across blocks, derive local source admission, and connect chronological store publication through assembly to the reference operator.
Construct an admitted grid schedule from supplied local cell executions with common entry arguments, without an assumed grid run or result.
Connect cell and assembly stores to fresh-residual subtraction, deriving input preservation and retaining the separate exact-real norm and stopping obligations.
Provide explicit necessary repeated-write visibility rules for in-place reductions, without claiming their full instruction correspondence.
Prove and bind the local rounded tree update as a reusable component of the complete native dot-output proof.
Connect shrinking reduction ownership to source selection and a completed two-stage example without claiming the full emitted reduction.

Derive shared-tree visibility for all 256 lanes from executed control and addresses; derive the native dot output and construct a complete admitted execution while keeping solver composition explicit.
Prove shared-tree numerical correctness and construct complete admitted executions for arbitrary initial words, with memory bounds; the full emitted dot-product entry remains separate.

Recover every returned lane’s rounded input partial sum from the complete concurrent dot program and its actual byte sources; derive input footprints and output-address ownership, with the shared tree and final output now joined in the same actual execution.
Derive each actual initial shared store’s rounded partial sum and lane-specific address from the same admitted input execution, with an explicit shared-allocation bound.
Prove that every returned lane has passed all nine native tree barriers and that each completion has earlier real arrivals from every participant.
Derive actual native shared read sources, shrinking writer ranges and barrier paths, then prove every dot output equals the prescribed rounded reduction of its actual input-loop partial sums.

Establish complete native-entry execution existence alongside universal output correctness, while keeping remaining PCG kernels, host composition, full PTX admission and hardware conformance separate.

Construct a complete finite native dot execution, admit its actual input/tree/output history, prove every lane returns, and exhibit a numerically correct output store without assuming intermediate read values.
Recover the dot result in mathematically published global bytes, independently of store order, and preserve every byte outside its output word.

Prove the complete per-thread direction-update entry, active and padding execution existence, and exact 25-instruction binding; keep concurrent in-place admission and PCG composition explicit remaining work.
Use an explicit same-thread no-future byte-source constraint for in-place updates, with a counterexample demonstrating why compatibility alone is insufficient.

from.quote:
One group of GPU threads handles each square element. Successive contractions
apply the one-dimensional basis tables, with barriers separating shared-memory
intermediates. Products and sums use separate explicitly rounded binary64
instructions. Contributions are first written into disjoint element storage.
Every group thread reaches each barrier, including inactive matrix lanes.
A second kernel gives each global node one writer, which sums its incident
contributions in element order. This preserves a deterministic assembly order
without concurrent floating-point updates. Interior solves explicitly zero the
boundary entries; the unrestricted operator is also available for comparison.

def element(self,name,source):
        m=self.l.m
        body=f'setp.lt.u32 %live, %lane, {m*m};\ndiv.u32 %i, %lane, {m};\nrem.u32 %j, %lane, {m};\n'
        stages=[]
        stages.append(f'mad.lo.u32 %idx, %cell, {m*m}, %lane;\n'+self.load('cells','%node','%idx')+self.load(source,'%value','%node')+self.shared_store(0,'%value'))
        stages.append(self.dot(('B','%i','k'),(0,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(1,'%acc')+
                      self.dot(('D','%i','k'),(0,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(2,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot((1,'%i','k'),('D','%j','k'))+self.load('W','%c','%lane')+
                      'mul.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %c;\n'+self.shared_store(3,'%acc')+
                      self.dot((2,'%i','k'),('B','%j','k'))+self.load('W','%c','%lane')+
                      'mul.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %c;\n'+self.shared_store(4,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot(('B','k','%i'),(3,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(5,'%acc')+
                      self.dot(('D','k','%i'),(4,'k','%j'))+self.shared_store(6,'%acc'))
        stages.append(self.dot((5,'%i','k'),('D','k','%j'))+self.dot((6,'%i','k'),('B','k','%j'),'%acc2')+
                      f'add.rn.f64 %value, %acc, %acc2;\nmad.lo.u32 %idx, %cell, {m*m}, %lane;\n'+self.store('element','%value','%idx'))
        for i,stage in enumerate(stages):
            body+=f'@!%live bra stage_{i}_done;\n'+stage+f'stage_{i}_done:\n'
            if i<len(stages)-1:body+='bar.sync 0;\n'
        return self.entry(name,body,32,self.l.n**2,7*m*m*8)
    def assemble(self,name,target,mask):
        body=self.vector_start()+self.load('offsets','%cursor','%global')+'add.u32 %idx, %global, 1;\n'+self.load('offsets','%end','%idx')
        body+=f'mov.f64 %acc, {ZERO};\nloop:\nsetp.ge.u32 %p0, %cursor, %end;\n@%p0 bra done;\n'
        body+=self.load('entries','%idx','%cursor')+self.load('element','%a','%idx')+'add.rn.f64 %acc, %acc, %a;\nadd.u32 %cursor, %cursor, 1;\nbra loop;\ndone:\n'
        if mask:body+=self.load('boundary','%flag','%global')+f'setp.ne.u32 %p0, %flag, 0;\n@%p0 mov.f64 %acc, {ZERO};\n'
        return self.entry(name,body+self.store(target,'%acc','%global'))

from.quote:
Vector updates, division by the Jacobi diagonal, dot products and square roots
are implemented in PTX. Dot products use a specified parallel reduction tree.
Their order can differ from the CPU reference, so numerical agreement is tested
rather than assumed bitwise. The loop retains active and broken state, freezes
updates after recursive convergence, recomputes the true residual at scheduled
checks and at the iteration limit, and restarts if the recursive test was too
optimistic. Empty interiors, zero loads, breakdown and exhausted iterations have
explicit outcomes. The recorded suite does not exercise a restart; implementation
of that branch does not imply observed coverage.

Generation validates the uniform connectivity, finite setup arrays, positive
interior diagonal, solver controls and a bounded 32-bit index domain. Device
storage contains guard bytes around every buffer; inputs and guards are checked
after solving. These checks and sanitizer runs support the tested executions,
not a universal memory-safety theorem.

Validation covers Q1–Q4, numerical operator comparisons on supplied and varied
vectors, complete solves, polynomial reproduction, boundary preservation,
iteration limits and invalid inputs. CPU references and device results start
from identical setup arrays. Saved cases, PTX and binary hashes, launch records,
outputs, toolchain identity and sanitizer logs make the observations reproducible.
All failures remain visible; tolerances are declared before running comparisons.
No throughput or benchmarking claim is part of this backend.

The numerical comparison uses fixed absolute and relative tolerances. Rounded
GPU and Lean residual measurements remain diagnostic comparisons and allow a
small measurement discrepancy. Acceptance additionally requires the proved
exact Lean residual checker: the saved setup coefficients and returned solution
must satisfy the requested bound with no extra allowance and exactly zero
boundary values. Iteration-limit and breakdown results are not certified.

            residual=math.hypot(*(a-b for a,b,bd in zip(ref['load'],independent['applied'],ref['boundary'],strict=True) if not bd))
            if math.isfinite(residual)!=math.isfinite(observed['true_residual_norm']) or (math.isfinite(residual) and abs(residual-observed['true_residual_norm'])>2e-12+2e-10*residual):
                raise AssertionError('reported residual disagrees with independently applied Lean operator')
            if observed['converged'] and residual>observed['tolerance']+2e-12:

For assembly, every recorded store has its owner's node address, independently
of proposed read values. Input arrays occupy byte ranges disjoint from the
output vector; either physical order is allowed. The actual offset-load
addresses therefore force their bytes to initialization. The resulting cursor
bounds constrain each contribution-index load, whose admitted bytes in turn
bound the cell-value address. This dependency order derives every read footprint
from the same joint history and discharges the replay separation condition.
No desired cursor range, read value or local snapshot execution is assumed.

compatible initialization sources. Each scalar execution reads its inputs
before its sole output store. Its recorded reads therefore use initial bytes;

from.quote:
The cell-to-assembly theorem uses the operator's actual connectivity arrays.
A finite checker decodes ordered contribution rows from the uploaded integer
tables. Actual cell executions share one initial global memory; their stores
are confined to their own active output coordinates and preserve assembly
metadata. Publishing these histories and executing assembly produces the
TorchLean tensor operator with the same rounded addition order and optional
boundary mask. A nonzero complete-cell and assembly example checks the
connection without supplying expected intermediate values.

theorem cell_assembly_operator {o : Operator} {values : Array Float}
    {words : List (Concurrent.Event o.mesh.points.size)}
    {indices : List (Fin o.mesh.points.size × IndexSources.Access)}
    {final : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Flow.State}
    (family : CellWhole.Family o values) (shape : OperatorMesh o)
    (same : o.q.size=o.nodes.size)
    (order : List (Fin o.mesh.cells.size)) (complete : ∀ i, i∈order)
    (a : Assembly.Arena o.mesh.points.size)
    (base : a.base=family.base) (element : a.element=family.output)
    (offsetsBefore : a.offsets.toNat+(o.mesh.points.size+1)*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (entriesBefore : a.entries.toNat+a.entryCount*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (boundaryBefore : a.boundary.toNat+o.mesh.points.size*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (tables : a.RowsEncoded family.memory (Assembly.nodeRows o.mesh.points.size (Assembly.MeshRows.locations shape.connectivity)))
    (separated : a.InputSeparation)
    (regs : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Registers)
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (Assembly.entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 o.mesh.points.size) a.offsets a.entries a.element mask a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start (family.publish family.memory order) (regs i)) words indices final)
    (compatible : Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible
      (fun space => match space with | .global => family.publish family.memory order | .shared => fun _ => 0) words wordSource)
    (indexCompatible : IndexSources.Compatible (family.publish family.memory order) words indices indexSource)
    (done : ∀ i, (final i).halted=true) (node : Fin o.mesh.points.size) :
    decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish (family.publish family.memory order) words) (Assembly.Snapshot.address a node))=
      if mask=true ∧ read32 family.memory (a.base.toNat+a.boundary.toNat+node.val*4)≠0 then 0 else
        shape.operator same values node := by
  rw [← family.input_word32 family.memory order (a.base.toNat+a.boundary.toNat+node.val*4)
    (by rw [base]; have := node.isLt; omega)]
  apply a.parallel_operator shape.connectivity
    (CoefficientRepresentation.rows same o.b) (CoefficientRepresentation.rows same o.d)
    (CoefficientRepresentation.square same o.w) (OperatorMesh.input values)
    run compatible indexCompatible (family.assembly_tables family.memory order a base offsetsBefore entriesBefore tables)
    separated done
  intro cell i j
  rw [CoefficientRepresentation.local_action,← shape.gather]
  have result := family.published_entry family.memory order cell (complete cell) i j
  unfold Assembly.Arena.elementValue
  rw [base,element]
  simpa only [CellWhole.Family.address,Nat.add_mul,Nat.add_assoc,Nat.add_left_comm,Nat.add_comm] using result

The executable array reference and the tensor operator now have a proved
connection. The actual reference loops enumerate cells and local coordinates
in the same order and perform the same rounded updates. With valid finite input,
the public Poisson.apply function returns exactly the vector published by the

theorem cell_assembly_reference {o : Operator} {values : Array Float}
    {words : List (Concurrent.Event o.mesh.points.size)}
    {indices : List (Fin o.mesh.points.size × IndexSources.Access)}
    {final : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Flow.State}
    (family : CellWhole.Family o values) (shape : OperatorMesh o)
    (same : o.q.size=o.nodes.size)
    (order : List (Fin o.mesh.cells.size)) (complete : ∀ i, i∈order)
    (a : Assembly.Arena o.mesh.points.size)
    (base : a.base=family.base) (element : a.element=family.output)
    (offsetsBefore : a.offsets.toNat+(o.mesh.points.size+1)*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (entriesBefore : a.entries.toNat+a.entryCount*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (boundaryBefore : a.boundary.toNat+o.mesh.points.size*4≤family.output.toNat)
    (tables : a.RowsEncoded family.memory (Assembly.nodeRows o.mesh.points.size (Assembly.MeshRows.locations shape.connectivity)))
    (separated : a.InputSeparation)
    (regs : Fin o.mesh.points.size → Registers)
    (run : Flow.Parallel.Runs a.context
      (Assembly.entryCode (BitVec.ofNat 32 o.mesh.points.size) a.offsets a.entries a.element false a.boundary a.output)
      (fun i => a.start (family.publish family.memory order) (regs i)) words indices final)
    (compatible : Concurrent.Visibility.Compatible
      (fun space => match space with | .global => family.publish family.memory order | .shared => fun _ => 0) words wordSource)
    (indexCompatible : IndexSources.Compatible (family.publish family.memory order) words indices indexSource)
    (done : ∀ i, (final i).halted=true)
    (size : values.size=o.mesh.points.size) (finite : values.all Float.isFinite=true) :
    Poisson.apply o values=.ok (Array.ofFn fun node : Fin o.mesh.points.size =>
      decode (read64 (Concurrent.GlobalPublication.publish (family.publish family.memory order) words)
        (Assembly.Snapshot.address a node))) := by
  rw [ArrayOperator.apply_correspondence o shape same values size finite]
  congr 1
  apply congrArg Array.ofFn
  funext node
  have result := cell_assembly_operator family shape same order complete a base element
    offsetsBefore entriesBefore boundaryBefore tables separated regs run compatible indexCompatible done node
  simpa only [Bool.false_eq_true,false_and,ite_false] using result.symm

theorem correct (run : NativeGuard.Runs cfg program s events t)
    (clean : ∀ u, s.pending u=false)
    (reset : s.core.barrier=Ptx.Barrier.reset generation)
    (entry : ∀ u, (s.core.lanes u).pc=0)
    (baseReg : ∀ u, ((s.core.lanes u).regs 3).toNat=base)
    (laneReg : ∀ u, ((s.core.lanes u).regs 14).toNat=u.val)
    (inputs : ∀ u, decode ((s.core.lanes u).regs 8)=input u.val)
    (noWrap : base+2048≤2^64)
    (compatible : Visibility.Compatible initialMemory events source)
    (ordered : OrderedSources events source)
    (done : ∀ u, (t.core.lanes u).pc=program.length) :
    ∃ (w : Nat) (access : Access), events[w]?=some (.data 0 access) ∧
      access.data.pc=66 ∧ access.data.store=true ∧ access.space=.shared ∧
      access.data.address=base ∧ decode access.data.value=Binary64.reduce256 input := by
  have ready : NativeGuard.Ready program s := ⟨by simp [clean],laneReg⟩
  have projection := (NativeGuard.project run ready frames.2 counts (by decide +kernel)).1
  exact Numeric.completed_result projection reset entry baseReg laneReg inputs noWrap compatible ordered done

theorem input_correct
    (run : Flow.Runs ctx (inputProgram count left right scratch) s t)
    (pc : s.core.pc=0) (running : s.halted=false) (done : t.core.pc=20)
    (bounded : count<2^30) (arrays : Arrays (setup ctx scratch s).core count left right) :
    decode (t.core.regs 8)=partialSum ctx scratch s count left right ∧
      Stable (setup ctx scratch s).core t.core := by
  obtain ⟨steps,counted⟩ := Flow.counted run
  obtain ⟨remaining,afterSetup⟩ := consume_setup counted pc running done
  have setupPC : (setup ctx scratch s).core.pc=(setupCode scratch).length := by
    simp [setup,setupCode,assign,advance,pc]
  obtain ⟨_,ready,_,traverse,exit,_,rest⟩ := Flow.OperandWindow.cut afterSetup setupPC running
    (by simp [done,setupCode,body,loadCode,addressCode])
  have readyPC : ready.core.pc=20 := by simpa [setupCode,body,loadCode,addressCode] using exit
  have finalEq := no_continuation rest (by
    change (inputProgram count left right scratch)[ready.core.pc]?=none
    rw [readyPC,← input_length (count:=count) (left:=left) (right:=right) (scratch:=scratch)]; simp)
  rw [finalEq]
  have result := traversal_correct traverse bounded (stable_refl _)
    (fun i hi => arrays_valid arrays bounded hi)
  simpa only [partialSum,setup_cursor,setup_zero] using result

from.quote:
For every returned thread, the proof recovers its actual input execution from
the interleaving. Other threads and later instructions leave this recorded
input execution unchanged. Every retained read is connected to the original
whole-kernel memory history. The unsigned loop guard and address instructions
prove that each read belongs to one of the input arrays. Every global store in
the complete entry is proved to use the designated output address. When that
word is disjoint from the inputs, byte-source compatibility forces every input
read to recover its initialized bytes. Thus the lane's rounded partial sum
follows from actual execution and memory admission, without a supplied read
value, partial-sum equation, local execution or phase boundary.

theorem completed_input_correct
    (whole : NativeFlow.Runs cfg ctx (program count left right output scratch) start events allIndices final)
    (aligned : Aligned start.core) (entry : ∀ thread, (start.core.lanes thread).pc=0)
    (live : start.halted owner=false) (returned : final.halted owner=true)
    (arena : ∀ thread, (ctx thread).arena=base)
    (sameInitial : (start.core.lanes owner).global=initial .global)
    (compatible : Visibility.Compatible initial events source)
    (bounded : count<2^30) (apart : OutputApart count left right output)
    (arrays : DotInput.Arrays (DotInput.setup (ctx owner) scratch (NativeFlow.lane start owner)).core count left right)
    (outputFits : base.toNat+output.toNat+8≤2^64) :
    ∃ next words indices,
      Flow.Observed.Runs (ctx owner) (DotInput.inputProgram count left right scratch)
        (NativeFlow.lane start owner) words indices next ∧
      (∀ a∈words, Event.data owner a∈events) ∧
      Flow.Runs (ctx owner) (DotInput.inputProgram count left right scratch)
        (NativeFlow.lane start owner) next ∧ next.core.pc=20 ∧ next.halted=false ∧
      decode (next.core.regs 8)=DotInput.partialSum (ctx owner) scratch (NativeFlow.lane start owner) count left right ∧
      DotInput.Stable (DotInput.setup (ctx owner) scratch (NativeFlow.lane start owner)).core next.core := by
  obtain ⟨next,words,indices,observed,done,stillLive,recorded,_⟩ :=
    completed_input whole aligned (entry owner) live returned
  have room := arrays_room arrays
  rw [arena owner] at room
  have scalar := admitted_input whole aligned entry arena sameInitial compatible observed recorded
    bounded apart room outputFits
  have result := DotInput.input_correct scalar (entry owner) live done bounded arrays
  exact ⟨next,words,indices,observed,recorded,scalar,done,stillLive,result⟩

The first shared publication is connected to that same thread's admitted
input traversal. A stronger projection tracks the recovered registers until
the actual store: only the two temporary address registers may change. The
shared base, lane number and accumulator therefore come from the executed
setup and input calculation. The two address instructions produce the lane's
own eight-byte slot. With a lane number below 256 and an aligned, nonwrapping
2048-byte shared allocation, the store is within bounds. Its decoded word is
that lane's ordered rounded partial sum; neither the word nor a shared-memory
snapshot is supplied as a premise.

theorem publication_contents

The complete native dot entry derives the shared tree's read sources and
numerical values from its own execution. The input loop may revisit instructions,
but each shared-memory instruction occurs at most once per lane. Setup fixes
the shared base and lane number. Actual comparisons and branches restrict each
successive stage to half as many lanes, and actual address instructions keep
each writer in its own eight-byte slot. A later read has an earlier publication
connected through the same barrier's arrival and completion events. Lane
ownership and instruction order exclude stale or competing publications.
Consequently each read obtains the required preceding word, and each actual
rounded addition produces the next tree value. The last shared read obtains
lane zero's final publication; the output-address instructions preserve that
word until the global store. The resulting decoded output is the prescribed
binary64 reduction of the actual input-loop partial sums. Neither input sums,
shared snapshots, desired read values nor phase boundaries are assumed.

theorem tree_read_source {cfg : Config 256} {ctx : Fin 256 → Kernel.Context} {r : Nat}
    (run : NativeFlow.Runs cfg ctx (program count left right output scratch) start events indices final)
    (reset : start.core.barrier=Ptx.Barrier.reset generation)
    (entry : ∀ thread, (start.core.lanes thread).pc=0)
    (laneMap : ∀ thread, (ctx thread).lane.toNat=thread.val)
    (noWrap : scratch.toNat+2048≤2^64)

      events[w]?=some (.data writer wa) ∧ wa.data.pc=storeSite ⟨phase.val,by omega⟩ ∧
      wa.data.store=true ∧ wa.space=.shared ∧ Visibility.Across events w r ∧
      access.data.value=wa.data.value ∧ ∀ k, source r k=.store w k := by
  have aligned : Aligned start.core := by intro t h; simp [reset,Ptx.Barrier.reset] at h
  obtain ⟨read,shared,active,within,address⟩ := tree_read_layout run aligned entry laneMap noWrap
    (List.mem_of_getElem? observed) phase neighbor site
  let writer : Fin 256 := ⟨reader.val+readOffset phase neighbor,within⟩
  have writerActive : writer.val<Reduction.active ⟨phase.val,by omega⟩ := by
    rw [stride_double]
    change reader.val+readOffset phase neighbor<2*stride phase

    rw [site]; unfold barrierSite readPC; cases neighbor <;> simp

  have suffix : ∀ stage, 20≤storeSite stage := by intro stage; simp [storeSite]; omega
  have address' : access.data.address=scratch.toNat+writer.val*8 := address
  have value : access.data.value=wa.data.value ∧ ∀ k, source r k=.store w k := by

A complete native dot execution can be constructed from valid launch data.
Each lane executes its input loop from the common initialized global bytes.
The lanes then execute their initial shared stores, all nine real barrier
rounds, the actual comparison and branch instructions, and the reduction
updates. Nonzero lanes return after the final barrier; lane zero reads the
last shared publication, writes the global output and returns. The chosen
schedule is finite and may run lane bodies in sequence. It inserts no extra
barrier and does not replace shared reads with a local memory snapshot.

The construction retains every actual memory and barrier event. Global input
reads name initialization. Each shared read names the appropriate actual store;
its barrier path, lane ownership and instruction order exclude competing writes.
Byte compatibility and the fragment's ordered-source constraints hold for that
same combined history. The execution contains a real output store, and the
universal numerical theorem proves its decoded word equals the prescribed
binary64 reduction of the computed input-loop partial sums. This establishes
existence as well as conditional output correctness for the native dot entry.
It does not establish progress for every GPU schedule, full PTX memory admission,
or hardware conformance. Remaining PCG kernels and host launch composition are
separate obligations.

    (sameInitial : ∀ thread, (start.core.lanes thread).global=initial .global)
    (arena : ∀ thread, (ctx thread).arena=base)
    (laneMap : ∀ thread, (ctx thread).lane.toNat=thread.val)
    (bounded : count<2^30)
    (arrays : ∀ thread, DotInput.Arrays (DotInput.setup (ctx thread) scratch (NativeFlow.lane start thread)).core count left right)
    (aligned : scratch.toNat%8=0)

    ∃ final events indices source access,
      NativeFlow.Runs cfg ctx (program count left right output scratch) start events indices final ∧
      (∀ t, final.halted t=true) ∧ Visibility.Compatible initial events source ∧
      Visibility.Repeated.OrderedSources events source ∧ Event.data 0 access∈events ∧
      access.data.pc=102 ∧ access.data.store=true ∧ access.space=.global ∧

theorem admitted {cfg : Config 256} {ctx : Fin 256 → Kernel.Context}
    (run : NativeFlow.Runs cfg ctx (program count left right output scratch) start events indices final)
    (reset : start.core.barrier=Ptx.Barrier.reset generation)
    (entry : ∀ thread, (start.core.lanes thread).pc=0)
    (laneMap : ∀ thread, (ctx thread).lane.toNat=thread.val)

    ∃ source, Visibility.Compatible initial events source ∧ OrderedSources events source := by
  have stored : ∀ (w : Nat) (owner : Fin 256) (wa : Access), events[w]?=some (.data owner wa) →
      ∀ phase : Fin 9, wa.data.pc=storeSite phase → wa.data.value=words input phase.val owner.val := by
    intro w owner wa found phase position
    have props := Numeric.store_properties run found phase position
    rcases expected _ (List.mem_of_getElem? found) with global | tree | tail
    · have read := global.1
      rw [props.1] at read; contradiction
    · exact tree.2.2.2.1 phase position
    · rcases tail.2.2 with shared | global
      · have read := shared.2.1
        rw [props.1] at read; contradiction
      · have impossible := global.1.symm.trans props.2

The search-direction update has a complete per-thread fetched proof. Each
active thread executes the real launch-parameter and index setup, loads scalar
β and its old p and z words, computes the separately rounded product β · p,
adds z, stores the result and returns. Every other byte remains unchanged.
Padding threads return without memory accesses. Valid allocations give finite
execution witnesses for both paths. The 25-instruction Lean program is compared
with the emitted update_p entry, including the product register, scalar address,
in-place output address and unsigned guard. This establishes the per-thread
instruction result, not yet its concurrent in-place source admission or the
full PCG loop.

from.quote:
In-place updates need a source rule beyond byte compatibility. For synchronous
same-thread accesses using ordinary addresses and the generic memory proxy,
PTX causality forbids a read from taking bytes from a later overlapping store.
The restricted rule is explicit: it applies to actual same-thread occurrence
order at the same word address. If ownership excludes other writers, it forces
the old value to come from initialization. It does not order unrelated threads
or cover aliases, asynchronous accesses or the full PTX memory model. A
kernel-checked counterexample shows that byte compatibility alone accepts a
circular read justified by its own later write; the new rule rejects it.
Concurrent direction-update ownership and source proofs remain to be supplied.

theorem before_own_writes_initial
    (compatible : Compatible initial events source) (admitted : GlobalThreadSources events source)
    (observed : events[r]?=some (.data reader ra)) (read : ra.data.store=false) (global : ra.space=.global)
    (writers : ∀ (w : Nat) (owner : Fin n) (wa : Access), events[w]?=some (.data owner wa) →
      wa.data.store=true → wa.space=.global → ∀ j k : Fin 8,
      wa.data.address+j.val=ra.data.address+k.val → owner=reader ∧ r<w ∧ wa.data.address=ra.data.address) :
    (∀ k, source r k=.initial) ∧ ra.data.value=read64 (initial .global) ra.data.address := by
  have chosen : ∀ k, source r k=.initial := by
    intro k
    have byteSource := compatible r reader ra observed read k
    cases picked : source r k with
    | initial => rfl
    | store w j =>
      rw [picked] at byteSource
      obtain ⟨owner,wa,found,write,space,address,value⟩ := byteSource
      have sharedSpace := space.trans global
      obtain ⟨same,later,wordAddress⟩ := writers w owner wa found write sharedSpace j k address
      subst owner
      exact False.elim (admitted r w reader ra wa observed found read write global sharedSpace wordAddress.symm later j k address picked)
  refine ⟨chosen,?_⟩
  apply Sources.word_eq_of_bytes
  intro k
  have byteSource := compatible r reader ra observed read k
  simpa only [chosen k,global,Sources.byte_read64] using byteSource
